column71: The Anger Solutions for Youth program is an 8 week series that incorporates several evidence-based therapeutic models from Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Reality Therapy, Solution Focused Therapy, Behaviour Therapy, Art/Music Therapy tools and the Psychosocial Rehabilitation Model for life skills training. column146: DefinitionsPersonal Health Information (PHI) as defined in the Personal Health Information Protection Act, November 2004 (PHIPA):Personal health information....means identifying information about an individual whether oral or recorded, if the information,a) relates to the physical or mental health of the individual, including information that consists of the health history of the individual's family,b) relates to the provision of health care to the individual, including the identification of a person as a provider of health care to the individual, orc) is the individual's health number.Personally Identifiable Information: (PII) consists of any information which may be used to identify an individual.  Safeguarding privacy in a mobile workplace, Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario, p.2.Statement of Privacy of Personal InformationPathways Health Centre for Children collects and uses personally identifiable information and personal health information as an employer and as a provider of professional services to clients.Provincial legislation and statutes and professional ethics require that Pathways protect the personally identifiable information and personal health information of staff and employees.  Pathways' privacy practices comply with and are consistent with Ontario's Personal Health Information Protection Act (PHIPA) and the requirements of the Regulated Health Professions Act (RHPA).  Pathways, as a health information custodian, protects the personal health information in our custody against unauthorized use and disclosure in compliance with the Personal Health Information Protection Act, November 2004.The Centre has a written Commitment to Privacy (Attachment 1) to inform clients and their families of the Centre's practices relating to their personal health information.All employees, consultants, students, and volunteers are required to sign a confidentiality agreement upon initiation of their employment or engagement with Pathways.Pathways Health Centre for Children collects demographic, family, health history information and records of past services at home or in the community.  Pathways collects only the information about clients and their families that is necessary to assess the client and plan and deliver appropriate services.  Pathways may use this information to inform clients or their families about the activities of Pathways, including programs, services, special events, funding needs, volunteer and donation opportunities and donation receipts.Pathways stores and uses personal information and personal health information within electronic databases and networks.Pathways will not share the personal information about employees, clients or their families with any outside person or agency without the consent of the employee, client or the client's parent or legal guardian, unless we are required by law to do so.Pathways has identified a staff person as Privacy Officer for Pathways.Safeguarding Personal Health Information or Personally Identifiable InformationPROCEDURES - ON-SITE? all confidential information must be stored in a secure work area or in locked file drawers? at the end of the work day, clear all confidential information off your desk, printer tray, etc.? materials with confidential information are distributed to and shared with other staff on a need-to-know basis only? staff access client information only for the clients for whom they have responsibility? Pathways has the right and ability to audit access to client files? extra copies of confidential information are shredded after they have served their use? use staff hanging folders to share personal client information with another employee? place personal employee information into envelopes when sharing with another employee? discuss confidential client or employee information in a private place where one cannot be overheardPROCEDURES - OFF-SITECentral (official) employee and client records must not leave the Centre premises, except under the following circumstances:  ? in compliance of a court order or subpoena, or? in the custody of an agent of the Centre, under contractual agreements to securely dispose of records in compliance with the Centre's retention schedule, or? in the custody of an agent of the Centre, under contractual agreements to securely transport the records for the purposes of imaging them for compact storage, in compliance with the Centre's retention schedule.Electronic personal health information or personally identifiable information must be encrypted (regardless of medium) if it is taken or stored outside Pathways premises.  Staff are to use the remote password-protected and encrypted connection to the client information on the Centre's servers, whenever feasible, when they need to access client or employee information from outside the Centre.  (See Policy II.190 - Password Privacy and Security and Policy II.76 - Information Management.)Working files (paper):  It is the responsibility of the individual staff person to keep any personal health information or personally identifiable information in their files in a secure manner to protect the confidentiality of the information.  Paper files taken outside Pathways premises must be ? kept concealed, such as in the trunk of a car rather than the back seat? kept in a locked container, for example, briefcase, suitcase? limited in the amount of information taken in a working fileTelephone Communication Procedures? never leave sensitive or confidential information as a message on voice mail or answering machines? do not mention or discuss identifying client information or sensitive topics while talking on cell phones or in any public placeLimits to ConfidentialityClient information, including clinician's notes and working files, may be the subject of a subpoena at any time. Client information may be reviewed for quality in an accreditation or quality management process.  In the case of Accreditation, surveyors are required to sign a Confidentiality Agreement.ResearchPersonal Health Information may be disclosed to a researcher with the consent of the legal guardian provided the research plan has been approved by a Pathways Research Review Committee, in compliance with PHIPA sections 37 and 44. It is not a breach of confidentiality to report client information in a research study as long as the client is not identifiable.Education and Public RelationsThe client or the client's parent or legal guardian must consent to the use of photographs, films, sound recordings or other audio and/or visual reproductions for their use in educational or public relations opportunities.Breaches of Privacy of Personal InformationDefinition:  A breach occurs whenever a person has contravened or is about to contravene a provision of the Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004 (the Act)... This will generally be a situation where personal health information is stolen, lost, or accessed by unauthorized persons.  What to do When Faced With A Privacy Breach: Guidelines for the Health Sector http://www.ipc.on.ca/images/Resources/up-hprivbreach.pdf  (accessed November 26, 2008).A breach of personal health information (PHI) may include, but is not limited to:? failure to provide notice that personal health information (PHI) will be collected and used? obtaining PHI from an individual without following established consent procedures? sharing PHI with an unauthorized person beyond the established consent process or circle of care? using PHI for purposes other than those for which it was collected? unauthorized attempts to gain access to a Client Health Record, information system or its data? disposing of a Client Health Record in contravention of established retention policies? theft or other loss of an unencrypted laptop or portable drive or other device that contains confidential information? theft or loss of physical documents that contain confidential information? changes to information or a system's hardware, firmware or software characteristics without the knowledge, instruction or consent of the owner or Health Information CustodianIf personal health information or personally identifiable information is stolen, lost or accessed by unauthorized persons:? individual staff members must, upon learning of a breach of privacy, notify the Centre's Privacy Officer at the first reasonable opportunity? the Privacy Officer and senior individuals within the organization will evaluate the incident for the amount of risk involved, and? the Privacy Officer and senior individuals within the organization will address containment and notification requirements as outlined in Breach Notification Assessment Tool December 2006, Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for British Columbia and the Information and Privacy Commissioner for Ontario. ? column146: The collection of personal client information is important to providing quality health and social services offered at Carlington Community Health Centre. The protection of confidential and personal information is also very important. In accordance with Ontario's Personal Health Information Protection Act (PHIPA 2004), CCHC has taken additional steps to protect your privacy.For your protection we have ....Conducted a privacy impact assessment (PIA) to determine how well we are protecting your privacy;Approved a privacy policy and other related policies;Appointed a Privacy Officer; andSet up safeguards for handling paper, electronic and verbal personal health information.OUR COMMITMENTCarlington Community Health Centre is committed to protecting your personal health information. All staff, students and volunteers are committed to confidentiality.When your service provider collects information from you, it will only be what is needed to provide and enhance your care.Staff of CCHC work in teams to offer you with comprehensive care and service.  Information for your best care may be shared among those directly involved in your care.  We will not share information about you with others outside the centre without your permission, except under special circumstances (See Limits of Confidentiality).The information in your records belongs to you; the physical records themselves belong to us. You are welcome to access your records by contacting your service provider.  They will tell you the steps to take to access your information.  We will be responsive to any questions or complaints you may have regarding the protection of your privacy at CCHC or other service provider. LIMITS of CONFIDENTIALITYCarlington Community Health Centre must report information to third parties, without consent in these situations:·         If we believe that you are a physical danger to yourself or others·         If we suspect that a child under the age of 16 is at risk·         If our records are subpoenaed by the courts·         If you are considered by law to be unable to make informed decisions for yourself·         In cases of a communicable disease, required reporting to a public health agency·         To verify your eligibility to receive health care benefits·         In cases of required reporting to the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board·         To a Regulated Health Professional College in the event of an investigation.ACCESSING YOUR INFORMATIONIf you wish to access your records or make corrections to your records, write a note to your service provider with the date of your request, description of the information you wish to see, your signature and the signature of a witness.  We ask you deliver this letter in person, so that we can verify it is you making the request. An appointment will be set up for you and your service provider to review the records together.  If you need a copy of your records, let your service provider know in advance because we need time to prepare it.

column71:
L'équipe de crise mobile est un partenariat entre le service de police de Chatham-Kent et le Chatham-Kent Health Alliance (CKHA).

L'équipe a un gendarme entraîné par l'équipe HELP avec une infirmière en crise de santé mentale et de lutte contre les dépendances de CKHA. Ensemble, ils répondent aux incidents liés à la santé mentale et assurent un suivi en fournissant des évaluations psychiatriques appropriées pour les personnes présentes sur les lieux.

Ce concept d'équipe est un «modèle de premier répondant». Les agents de première ligne sélectionnés sont formés pour être en mesure de répondre 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7 aux situations où les personnes atteintes de maladie mentale sont en danger. De cette façon, nous sommes en mesure de mieux aider dans leur plus grand temps de besoin.

column2: Soins de santé primaires
column71:
Le CSC CHIGAMIK CHC offre des soins de santé primaires holistiques aux clients inscrits, en anglais et en français, y compris les services de : 

    • Personnel infirmier praticien
    • Médecins de famille
    • Personnel infirmier autorisé
    • Travailleurs en santé communautaire
    • Diététistes
    • Agents de promotion de la santé
    • Conseillers en santé mentale et en toxicomanie
    • Psychologues

Les services holistiques et adaptés à la culture que nous offrons sont fondés sur la philosophie des soins centrés sur le client et sur la notion d'habilitation individuelle et communautaire. Les clients de la clinique sont confiés à un médecin de famille ou à un membre du personnel infirmier praticien ou les deux, et reçoivent les soins du personnel infirmier. Voici quelques-uns des services que nous offrons :

    • Soins prénatal et postnatal
    • Services de santé mentale
    • Soins des pieds
    • Soins aux personnes âgées dans la communauté
    • Soins intégrés des maladies comme le diabète
    • Télémédecine par le biais du Réseau Télémédecine Ontario (RTO)
column75:
Les services de soins de santé primaires sont offerts à toute personne sans médecin de famille ou sans personnel infirmier praticien qui habite:
.Ile aux Chrétiens
.Midland
.Penetanguishene
.Tay
.Tiny

Nous sommes heureux d'offrir des soins bilingues et adaptés à la culture. Nous encourageons les personnes qui s'auto-identifient comme membre des Premières Nations, Métis, Inuit (PNMI) ou Francophone et qui habitent les municipalités ci-dessus ou ailleurs dans la région de Simcoe Nord Muskoka à s'inscrire comme client. Votre cercle de soins est forme d'une équipe clinique et de professionnels connexes de la santé. À titre de client, vous avez accès a l'équipe interdisciplinaire sous un seul toi!

Si vous répondez à nos critères ou que c'est le cas d'une personne que vous connaissez, veuillez communiquer avec nous!

N'oubliez pas - Vous pouvez toujours participer aux programmes de promotion de la santé, sans frais, même si vous n'êtes pas un client inscrit du CSC CHIGAMIK CHC. Pour y participer, vous devez être résident de l'île aux Chrétiens, Midland, Penetanguishene, Tay ou Tiny ou s'identifier comme membre des Premières nations, Métis, Inuit (PNMI) ou Francophone dans la région de Simcoe Nord Muskoka.

column146: DefinitionsPersonal Health Information (PHI) as defined in the Personal Health Information Protection Act, November 2004 (PHIPA):Personal health information....means identifying information about an individual whether oral or recorded, if the information,a) relates to the physical or mental health of the individual, including information that consists of the health history of the individual's family,b) relates to the provision of health care to the individual, including the identification of a person as a provider of health care to the individual, orc) is the individual's health number.Personally Identifiable Information: (PII) consists of any information which may be used to identify an individual.  Safeguarding privacy in a mobile workplace, Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario, p.2.Statement of Privacy of Personal InformationPathways Health Centre for Children collects and uses personally identifiable information and personal health information as an employer and as a provider of professional services to clients.Provincial legislation and statutes and professional ethics require that Pathways protect the personally identifiable information and personal health information of staff and employees.  Pathways' privacy practices comply with and are consistent with Ontario's Personal Health Information Protection Act (PHIPA) and the requirements of the Regulated Health Professions Act (RHPA).  Pathways, as a health information custodian, protects the personal health information in our custody against unauthorized use and disclosure in compliance with the Personal Health Information Protection Act, November 2004.The Centre has a written Commitment to Privacy (Attachment 1) to inform clients and their families of the Centre's practices relating to their personal health information.All employees, consultants, students, and volunteers are required to sign a confidentiality agreement upon initiation of their employment or engagement with Pathways.Pathways Health Centre for Children collects demographic, family, health history information and records of past services at home or in the community. column71: Offre un programme d'emploi rémunéré de 16 semaines permettant aux jeunes femmes et aux jeunes non-binaires développer et d'améliorer leurs compétences de vie et d'employabilité et de réussir leurs transitions sur le marché du travail. Comprend 4 semaines de formation payée suivies de 12 semaines de stage rémunéré. Offre une expérience de travail réelle aux personnes pour les aider à acquérir de l'expérience dans leur domaine, de démontrer leurs compétences et acquérir de nouvelles compétences.
column75: Les jeunes qui s'identifient comme étant des femmes ou des non-binaires âgés de 15 à 30 ans et qui ont besoin d'aide pour surmonter les obstacles à l'emploi. Doit être légalement autorisé à travailler au Canada et en Ontario et ne pas recevoir de prestations d'assurance-emploi (AE).
